messages:
Anna Li: FYI CVE-2026-XXXX — active exploit reports for spring-session cookie deserialization. seen in the wild. linking advisory: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-XXXX
sec-oncall: 🚨 Alerting oncall rotation. Priority: P0. Start incident page and post links to this thread.
Mike Rivera: Are we running spring-session anywhere in hosted / dedicated? I can run a quick inventory query.
Sophia Chen: I've started an automated scan against our artifact repo. quick note: spring-session is pulled transitively by legacy auth-service and a couple of vendor connectors.
Anna Li: Repro steps from advisory: attacker can craft a cookie payload to trigger deserialization. immediate mitigations: 1) patch libs, 2) block exploit pattern at WAF, 3) rotate session keys / invalidate sessions.
Kevin Patel: Oncall: I'll add a temporary RBAC restriction on deploys to auth-service and connectors until we have patches. who will create the patch PRs?
Mike Rivera: I can own auth-service patch. plan: upgrade to spring-session 3.2.1 (fix included) and run integration tests. ETA 2h for a PR, 4h for canary.
Sophia Chen: I'll push a WAF rule blocking the specific cookie header patterns and known payload markers. rule name: block_cve_2026_XXXX_cookie. Deploying in staged WAF first.
Anna Li: Ops: we need KMS rotation? The session signing keys are in KMS, not directly vulnerable, but rotating reduces blast radius for stolen cookies. Recommend scheduled key rotation + revoke active session tokens via cache flush.
Mike Rivera: For KMS: can we do a targeted key version and not full rotation? We use Google KMS; I'll trigger createKeyVersion + update app secret reference. need support from infra for zero-downtime key swap.
Sophia Chen: infra note: we can create new key version, update secret manager reference, then restart pods in canary groups. I'll coordinate with deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: @Sophia Chen initiating canary restart for auth-service in us-west-2. rolling 2/5 replicas.
Kevin Patel: Audit logging: Anna, please list the log patterns we want to search for. we'll run queries across ELK and retention buckets.
Anna Li: Search for base64 cookie strings with suspicious prefixes, deserialization exceptions in auth-service logs, and any 5xx spikes from session handling. example query: 
```
message: \"DeserializeException\" AND service:auth-service AND cookie:*session*
```
Also look for IPs with multiple cookie attempts.
Mike Rivera: I'll add a quick health-check patch to ensure new library doesn't regress on session expiry semantics.
Sophia Chen: ETA for WAF rule in prod: 20m after staging verification.
Anna Li: Communications: we should send an internal advisory to CS and trust. Also prepare a customer-facing FAQ if we need to notify. Draft: "We identified and patched a vulnerability in a session library; we have mitigations in place and no evidence of customer data exfiltration."
Kevin Patel: I'll open an incident doc and stakeholder page, assign comms to @marketing after we have confirmation.
Mike Rivera: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/auth-service/pulls/1423 — bump spring-session, tests passing locally. tagging @Sophia Chen for deploy.
Sophia Chen: Reviewing PR now. If tests look good I'll canary deploy to one region and monitor audit logs for any DeserializeException increases.
Anna Li: Post-mitigation checks: 1) confirm no DeserializeExceptions in last 6h, 2) ensure session invalidation occurred, 3) confirm key rotation completed.
Kevin Patel: Action items recap: Mike patch + canary, Sophia WAF + deploy, Anna audit queries + comms draft, infra assist with KMS key version swap.
Mike Rivera: Starting the canary deploy now.
Sophia Chen: Canary deployed to us-west-2, 1 replica. Monitoring: no new DeserializeExceptions in 10m, CPU/memory normal.
Anna Li: Great. keep the RBAC deploy restriction in place until all regions patched.
sec-oncall: Incident severity set to P0. Next update in 30m or on milestone. reactions: :rotating_light: :lock:
